features.feature_value: Used writing-style/tone cues (e.g., vulgarity, ALL CAPS) as a basis for keep/remove
features.evidence_span: "The level of vulgarity or the inappropriate writing style (e.g., ALL CAPS)."
features.rationale: The participant explicitly ties their decisions to vulgarity and formatting/style markers.

features.feature_value: Kept most pairs; focused deletions on posts that add nothing except name calling/invective
features.evidence_span: "removing posts that added nothing to the conversation but name calling or invective"
features.rationale: They describe a specific deletion trigger centered on invective rather than the underlying claims.

features.feature_value: Considered threats of violence/hurting a person or group as the key line for removal
features.evidence_span: "Threats of violence... when it turns to hurting a person or group that's a big line crossed."
features.rationale: They draw the keep/remove boundary at violence/threats and harm to a group.

features.feature_value: Argued for limiting restrictions and allowing misinformation symmetrically (both directions) absent real measurable harm/incitement
features.evidence_span: "if misinformation is allowed in one direction it needs to be allowed in both directions"
features.rationale: They frame decisions around comparative symmetry between paired versions and a harm/rights threshold.

features.feature_value: Compared the paired posts on like-for-like rhetoric (hyperbole, unsourced claims, aggression) to avoid internal bias
features.evidence_span: "By pairing up rather than evaluating in isolation, I could compare..."
features.rationale: They describe using the pairing itself to keep standards constant and minimize bias.

features.feature_value: Used a fairness criterion—evaluating decisions as fair without being biased
features.evidence_span: "What was fair without being biased is how i evaluated each decision"
features.rationale: Their reflection directly states a fairness/no-bias evaluation principle.

features.feature_value: Chose deletions mainly for inflammatory content; otherwise left posts alone
features.evidence_span: "I only really opted to delete posts that were inflammatory. The rest seemed fine"
features.rationale: They specify a narrow decision rule: delete only when inflammatory.

features.feature_value: Allowed posts if not unnecessarily hateful/hostile, framing even disagreement as worth discussion
features.evidence_span: "I allowed them as long as they were not unnecessarily hateful/hostile"
features.rationale: They state keep conditions based on the presence/absence of hostility.
